c: Next article in this issue Introduction Global climate challenges and the threat they pose to modern societies have become central to both scientific and public discourse over the past few decades. A critical component in finding solutions to these challenges is addressing the oversized role carbon-heavy energy sources play in our current infrastructure [1], [2], [3], [4]. Following the 2021 United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP26), further climate goals were added with the EU collectively declaring that its energy mix will comprise of 55% renewable energy sources (RES) by 2050 [5]. The United States also pledged to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 50%–52% below 2005 levels by 2030, with this target being part of a broader commitment to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 [6].
